event: Oldest solids of the Solar System (CAIs); Earth formation bound
source: Connelly et al. 2012, Science; ICS chart v2024-12 (base of Hadean 4567)
note: CAIs date the Solar System at 4567.30 +/- 0.16 Ma; Earth itself accreted over tens of Myr after, so ma_lo uses Wilde 2001's 'about 4550 Ma' for Earth's formation.

event: Oldest zircon evidence for liquid water (Jack Hills)
source: Wilde et al. 2001, Nature; Valley et al. 2014, Nature Geoscience
note: Zircon age 4404 +/- 8 Ma; its oxygen isotopes are read as magma that interacted with a liquid hydrosphere. Age is firm (Valley 2014 re-confirmed ~4.4 Ga by atom-probe); the water inference is interpretive.

event: Oldest claimed (disputed) life: Nuvvuagittuq hematite tubes
source: Dodd et al. 2017, Nature
note: Putative microfossils in vent-type rocks at least 3770 Ma, possibly 4280 Ma; the 4280 age rests on a contested date for the host belt and biogenicity is challenged.

event: Claimed life: graphite in Jack Hills zircon
source: Bell et al. 2015, PNAS
note: Carbon inclusions (d13C -24 +/- 5 permil) in a 4.10 +/- 0.01 Ga zircon, called 'potentially biogenic' by the authors; single grain, not confirmed.

source: Tashiro et al. 2017, Nature
note: Light carbon isotopes in metamorphosed graphite, read as organisms older than 3.95 Ga (lower bound as stated).

source: Nutman et al. 2016, Nature
note: 1-4 cm layered structures in 3700 Ma metacarbonate read as microbial; interpretation of these structures has been contested (not checked in primary rebuttal here).

event: Oldest widely accepted life: Dresser Formation, Pilbara
source: Noffke et al. 2013, Astrobiology; Nutman et al. 2016, Nature (calls it the previous most convincing evidence)
note: Microbially induced sedimentary structures in ca. 3.48 Ga rocks; uncertainty not read from primary, so ma_lo/ma_hi equal ma.

source: Allwood et al. 2006, Nature; Wacey et al. 2011, Nature Geoscience
note: Seven stromatolite morphotypes in a ~3.43 Ga carbonate platform; biogenicity argued against abiotic models but debate continues.

source: Schopf et al. 2002, Nature; Brasier et al. 2002, Nature
note: Claimed microfossils; Brasier et al. 2002 (https://doi.org/10.1038/416076a) questioned them. Age ~3.465 Ga is from memory, not re-verified.

source: Moody et al. 2024, Nature Ecology & Evolution
note: Gene-duplicate molecular clock: ~4.2 Ga (4.09-4.33 Ga interval as stated in abstract, via Europe PMC PMC11383801); implies a genome >=2.5 Mb, ~2600 proteins. Betts 2018 gave LUCA >3.9 Ga.

source: Gumsley et al. 2017, PNAS; Luo et al. 2016, Science Advances
note: Onset placed ~2.46-2.43 Ga (Gumsley, per secondary summaries) vs sharp rise 2.33 Ga (Luo); later work says not synchronous. ICS Siderian/Rhyacian boundary = 2300 Ma.

event: Oldest eukaryote claim: Grypania, Negaunee Iron Formation
source: Han & Runnegar 1992, Science
note: Coiled ribbon read as megascopic alga in ~2.1 Ga rock; eukaryote assignment not secure (age is from title).

event: Oldest confident eukaryote fossils: Changcheng acritarchs
source: Betts et al. 2018, Nature Ecology & Evolution
note: Large, complex-walled acritarchs ~1.62 Ga treated as oldest confident eukaryotes; only give a minimum age for the eukaryote stem. Range is approximate.

source: Betts et al. 2018, Nature Ecology & Evolution
note: Modern (crown) eukaryotes emerged <1.84 Ga; mitochondrial symbiosis 2.053-1.21 Ga. ma_lo is the low end of the mitochondria interval, not of the crown date.

source: Betts et al. 2018, Nature Ecology & Evolution
note: Oldest fossil confidently assignable to crown Eukaryota (~1.1 Ga, per Betts summary).

event: Animals: molecular-clock origin of crown Metazoa
source: dos Reis et al. 2015, Current Biology; ICS chart v2024-12 (Cryogenian ~720-635 Ma)
note: Abstract only says crown Metazoa arose in the Cryogenian and that precision is limited. ma is the midpoint of the ICS Cryogenian bounds (arithmetic, not a paper result); numeric clock estimates not read.

source: Love et al. 2009, Nature; Antcliffe 2013, Palaeontology; Bobrovskiy et al. 2021, Nat Ecol Evol
note: Steranes read as demosponges at ~635 Ma; host-rock age questioned (645-~580 Ma) and compound shown possibly algal (Bobrovskiy 2021, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-020-01334-7).

event: Oldest accepted animals: Ediacara macrofossils (Dickinsonia sterols)
source: Bobrovskiy et al. 2018, Science
note: Abstract gives Ediacara biota as 571-541 Ma; Dickinsonia cholesteroids make them the oldest confirmed macroscopic animals. Dickinsonia samples ~558 Ma per press coverage only. 574 Ma (Avalon Charnia) from brief: not verified.

source: Evans et al. 2020, PNAS
note: Small mobile organism with front/back differentiation in the Ediacara Member, South Australia. Age ~555 Ma is from memory, not in abstract; range approximate.

source: ICS International Chronostratigraphic Chart v2024-12
note: Chart prints ~635 (approximate, no error term).

source: ICS International Chronostratigraphic Chart v2024-12
note: 538.8 +/- 0.6 Ma as printed on the chart (extracted from PDF text).

event: Oldest fossil brain: Fuxianhuia protensa, Chengjiang
source: Ma, Hou, Edgecombe & Strausfeld 2012, Nature
note: Preserved tripartite brain and optic neuropils in a stem arthropod, stated as 520 Ma; Chengjiang ~518 per secondary sources. This is a minimum age for nervous systems.

source: Shu et al. 1999, Nature
note: Jawless fish-like animals from Chengjiang (~518 Ma per secondary sources); yunnanozoans (Tian 2022, https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abm2708) argued as stem vertebrates but disputed.

source: Hublin et al. 2017 + Richter et al. 2017, Nature
note: 315 +/- 34 ka weighted age (Richter abstract), i.e. 0.315 Ma; 286 +/- 32 ka for Irhoud 3 tooth by US-ESR. Earliest-sapiens label depends on how 'sapiens' is defined.
